In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cis-regulatory components of the Hox cluster that are responsible for the segmental expression in neural tissue are not conserved between vertebrates and urochordate species.

cis-elements responsible for Hox expression in anterior neural tissue have been conserved in chordates, with the notable exception of the hindbrain where the Hox1-4 paralogous genes are regulated by Kreisler and/or Krox20 dependent cis-regulatory elements.
the Hox response element is a chordate innovation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulatory mechanisms controlling Hox gene expression have been maintained throughout chordate evolution.

the cis-regulatory mechanisms for the Hox response elements are conserved in the chordate lineage, whereas the cis-regulatory mechanism that is involved in segmental regulation is vertebrate specific.

the cis-elements we have characterized are part of a regulatory network that is shared by urochordate and vertebrate Hox genes and that this network is involved in the regulation of the expression domains of these genes along the anterior-posterior axis of the developing neural system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Hox regulatory sequences have been conserved across the chordate lineage, and that the regulatory components that recognize them have been maintained in the face of extensive morphological and genetic changes.
Hox response elements are conserved in chordates and that the cis-regulatory components involved in their activity have also been conserved.
cis-regulatory components have evolved to respond to Hox proteins, and this is a fundamental feature of Hox regulatory networks in the nervous system.
